back: The breakdown of rock in place (no transport) by physical, chemical or biological processes.
Freeze-thaw (ice expands about 9%), pressure release (exfoliation), thermal expansion and contraction (moisture-assisted) and salt crystallisation.
Hydrolysis (feldspar to clay), carbonation (limestone dissolved by carbonic acid), oxidation (iron oxides) and solution.
CaCO₃ + H₂O + CO₂ → Ca(HCO₃)₂: calcium carbonate becomes soluble calcium hydrogencarbonate.
A biological/chemical process in which organic compounds bind metal ions (iron, aluminium) and remove them from minerals, weakening the rock.
Graph of mean annual temperature against mean annual rainfall showing the dominant weathering: chemical in hot, wet climates; freeze-thaw in cold, moist climates; slow in dry ones.
Rule of thumb: the rate of a chemical reaction roughly doubles for every 10 °C rise in temperature (approximate).
Rock type and structure, relief, vegetation and human influence (quarrying, acid rain, clearing).
Percentage loss = (start mass − final mass) ÷ start mass × 100; divide by the number of years for the rate per year.
